about: Routes from outside (non-Adobe) systems into the products on the Build canvas, read from Adobe's documentation on November 2 2026 by five researchers (one per product group), each with the page URL and an exact quote. A second reader re-checks each route against its page; 'checked' holds those verdicts where they are done. Only checked routes go into the tool. See sow/canvas/OUTSIDE_SYSTEMS.md.

routes.mechanism: Experience Platform cloud storage source connector (batch files in XDM JSON, XDM Parquet or delimited format) into a dataset, then a CJA connection and data view
routes.partner_work: Per Adobe's CJA quick start for source connectors: create the XDM schema and dataset, then run the source workflow (authentication, select data, dataflow detail, mapping to the schema, scheduling, review). Add the dataset to a CJA connection (person ID, data source type, import all new data, backfill) and add its fields to a data view. Monitor the dataflows: Adobe disables source dataflows that fail continuously for 30 days.
routes.prerequisites: Included with a CJA license: the product description says non-Adobe sources may be configured into CJA through the UI and API. Experience Platform role with View Sources and Manage Sources to create the dataflow, plus sandbox access, View Schemas, Manage Schemas, View Datasets and View Identity Namespaces to create the CJA connection. For sources that pull from the client's systems, Adobe's region-specific IP addresses allowlisted on the client's side. CJA Foundation allows one event dataset per connection (profile, lookup and summary datasets are fine), so a second event source next to web data needs Select or higher.
routes.url_title: Ingest and use data using source connectors (Customer Journey Analytics Guide)
routes.quote: Cloud storage (source connectors include Amazon S3, Azure Blob, and more)
routes.notes: Full vendor list from the Experience Platform sources overview (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/home), which says 'Cloud storage sources can bring your own data into Experience Platform without the need to download, format, or upload.' Azure Blob and ADLS Gen2 do not support same-region connectivity to Experience Platform. Adobe's CJA Google Analytics backfill guide uses the Google Cloud Storage source. Overlaps the existing CJ01 line (CJA data preparation in Experience Platform), which covers ingestion in general rather than per source.

vendors: Data Landing Zone (Azure Blob container provisioned by Adobe; an Amazon S3 folder when Experience Platform runs on AWS)
routes.mechanism: Data Landing Zone source connector for file drops into Experience Platform; the Data Landing Zone is also a target for CJA full table export and for dataset export
routes.partner_work: Retrieve the sandbox's Data Landing Zone credentials from the sources catalog, set up the client's file transfer (Azure Storage Explorer with the SAS URL, the command line with AzCopy, an Azure Data Factory linked service, or the AWS console on AWS), follow Adobe's file and folder naming rules, create the dataflow with mapping and a schedule, then add the dataset to the CJA connection.
routes.prerequisites: Included with CJA: one Data Landing Zone per sandbox, total size capped by the client's Experience Platform storage, files deleted after 7 days, to be used only to move data into and out of Experience Platform. Private links are not supported. View Sources and Manage Sources permissions.
routes.url_title: Customer Journey Analytics | Product Description (effective 22 October 2026)
routes.quote: Customer will receive access to 1 Data Landing Zone per Sandbox.
routes.notes: Data Landing Zone source page (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/connectors/cloud-storage/data-landing-zone): 'Data Landing Zone is an Azure Blob storage interface provisioned by Adobe Experience Platform'. Product description: 'Data will automatically be deleted from the Data landing Zone after 7 days.' Useful when the client has no cloud storage of its own.

Snowflake, Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift, Azure Databricks and Azure Synapse Analytics are not in this group.

routes.mechanism: Experience Platform Data Mirror for CJA: warehouse source connector with change data capture into relational (Model-based) datasets that keep inserts, updates and deletes in sync
routes.partner_work: Per Adobe's Data Mirror quick start: enable change history on each warehouse table; create a relational schema (Time series for events, Record for profile and lookup data) with a primary key, a version descriptor and, for events, a timestamp descriptor; set up the Snowflake, BigQuery or Databricks source with Enable change data capture, map the fields and set the sync schedule; add the relational dataset to a CJA connection and set how it joins on a person ID or account ID; add the fields (Adhoc & relational fields folder) to the data view, merging same-named XDM fields with derived fields where needed; plan for deletes and data hygiene.
routes.prerequisites: CJA Select, Prime or Ultimate (the product description lists Data Mirror as not included in Foundation). Adobe's Experience Platform page calls it a limited release that depends on license and feature enablement, through the Adobe account team. Mirrored changes count against the CJA Annual Ingestion Limit. Warehouse credentials, IP allowlisting and change history enabled on the tables.
routes.quote: from external systems such as Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery directly into Experience Platform
routes.notes: Status conflict: the Experience Platform page (updated Oct 21 2026) carries a Limited Availability badge and says 'Data Mirror is available as a limited release for Customer Journey Analytics users, depending on your license and feature enablement.' The CJA 2026 release notes list Data Mirror with rollout March 25, 2026 and general availability June 17, 2026. CJA how-to: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/analytics-platform/using/cja-data-mirror/relational. Data Mirror is the one way a CJA license can use these warehouse connectors without a separate license. CJA ignores the relationship descriptors in relational schemas. B2B Edition account-based connections accept relational datasets since July 2026.

routes.mechanism: Advanced enterprise source connector (batch) into standard XDM datasets, without Data Mirror
routes.partner_work: Same source workflow as the other databases (credentials, IP allowlist, table or query selection, mapping, schedule), then the CJA connection and data view.
routes.prerequisites: Not included with CJA on its own: the CJA product description allows these connectors only as part of Data Mirror or when licensed separately. Adobe's sources overview lists them as available to Real-Time CDP Ultimate or with the standalone Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors SKU.
routes.url_title: Customer Journey Analytics | Product Description (effective 22 October 2026)
routes.quote: Customer may not import data from Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors unless used as part of AEP Data Mirror functionality or licensed separately.
routes.notes: Each of these source pages carries an Ultimate badge, for example BigQuery: 'The Google BigQuery source is available in the sources catalog to users who have purchased Real-Time Customer Data Platform Ultimate.' Adobe's CJA Google Analytics backfill guide sidesteps the BigQuery source by exporting to Google Cloud Storage and using that source.

routes.mechanism: Advanced enterprise streaming source connector into a dataset
routes.partner_work: Authenticate the stream, map incoming records with Data Prep, create the streaming dataflow, then add the dataset to the CJA connection and data view.
routes.prerequisites: Separate license: Adobe lists these as available only to Real-Time CDP Ultimate or with the standalone Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors SKU, and the CJA product description excludes advanced enterprise sources unless licensed separately.

routes.notes: Google PubSub: 'You can only create one source dataflow per Google PubSub subscription.' Snowflake streaming: 'The Snowflake streaming source is available in the API to users who have purchased Real-Time CDP Ultimate.' For a CJA-only client the HTTP API source is the included streaming route (next item).

routes.category: Custom app or system with no connector (streaming)
routes.mechanism: HTTP API streaming source connector: Experience Platform issues a streaming endpoint URL that the client application posts records to
routes.partner_work: Create the schema and dataset, create the HTTP API source under Sources > Streaming (XDM compatible, or raw data mapped with Data Prep), give the endpoint URL to the client's developers, validate the first records, then add the dataset to the CJA connection and data view.
routes.prerequisites: Included with CJA (HTTP API is not an advanced enterprise source). View Sources and Manage Sources. Developer work on the client side to send the records. Adobe asks for a 5-minute pause in ingestion after a streaming dataflow is created or updated.
routes.url_title: Ingest and use streaming data (Customer Journey Analytics Guide)
routes.quote: Use HTTP API source connector to easily stream your data into the dataset configured in Adobe Experience Platform.
routes.notes: Adobe names systems, not vendors. CJA data ingestion overview: 'That data source is able to communicate over HTTP or public cloud streaming infrastructure but for which Adobe currently does not provide a source connector.' HTTP API source page: 'The HTTP API source is supported by Data Prep functions, allowing you to map any non XDM-compliant data to an XDM-compliant dataset.'

routes.category: Flat file exports from systems with no connector
routes.mechanism: Batch upload with the Experience Platform workflow 'Map CSV to XDM schema' (or the Local file upload source) into a dataset
routes.partner_work: Model the file in an XDM schema (Individual Profile class for attributes, Experience Event for events), create the dataset, run Map CSV to XDM schema with AI-assisted mapping, calculated fields and mapping templates, preview, ingest, then add the dataset to the CJA connection. For recurring loads, move to a cloud storage source.
routes.prerequisites: Included with CJA (data ingestion tools are part of the license). Sandbox access with schema and dataset permissions. Adobe's quick start also turns on Real-Time Customer Profile for the schema and dataset, but the CJA product description does not license Profile Service unless it is licensed separately, so that step applies only to clients that also own Real-Time CDP.
routes.url_title: Data ingestion overview (Customer Journey Analytics Guide)
routes.quote: flat files in CSV, JSON, or Parquet format from a CRM system, loyalty application, or other solution
routes.notes: Step by step: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/analytics-platform/using/cja-data-ingestion/ingest-use-guides/batch (Adobe's example is a loyalty CSV with email, loyaltyID, points and status). The CJA product description: 'unless licensed separately, Customer is not licensed to, and must not, access or use Batch Query Service components, Data Science Workspace, Profile Service, or Segmentation Service components'.

routes.category: CSV lookup file without schema design (ad hoc)
routes.mechanism: Ad hoc dataset: Experience Platform builds the dataset and an ad hoc schema from the CSV, and CJA uses it as an event, profile, lookup or summary dataset
routes.partner_work: Create a dataset from the CSV in Experience Platform, add it to the connection with the right dataset type and keys (Adobe's example maps tracking codes to ad groups and campaign names), then add the fields to the data view.
routes.prerequisites: Included with CJA. Large lookups are not supported for ad hoc datasets.
routes.url_title: Ingest and use ad hoc data (Customer Journey Analytics Guide)
routes.quote: Create a dataset with a CSV file in Experience Platform.
routes.notes: Create connection page: 'Large lookups are not supported for Customer Managed Keys and Ad hoc datasets.' Ad hoc fields are 'namespaced for usage only by a single dataset'.

routes.category: Classification data (product catalog, campaign or content metadata)
routes.mechanism: Lookup dataset on a custom Record-class schema, loaded by CSV (Map CSV to XDM schema) or any other ingestion method, matched to a field in the connection
routes.partner_work: Create one custom Record-class schema and lookup dataset per dimension to classify, load the file and check the mappings, add the dataset to the connection with its key and matching key (up to three levels of lookups), then expose the classified fields in the data view.
routes.prerequisites: Included with CJA. Unique key strings per lookup dataset depend on the package: 10 million (Foundation), 100 million (Select), 250 million (Prime), one billion (Ultimate).
routes.url_title: Create lookup datasets to classify data in Customer Journey Analytics
routes.quote: Similar to classifications data in Adobe Analytics, lookup datasets are the method for classifying data in Customer Journey Analytics.
routes.notes: Same page: 'You could also use any other method available for importing data into Experience Platform, such as setting up a datastream.' Create connection page: 'You can add up to three levels of lookups.'

routes.mechanism: Summary dataset on an XDM Summary Metrics schema (hourly or daily), uploaded as CSV and joined to event data through a shared key such as a campaign tracking code
routes.partner_work: Create a schema on the XDM Summary Metrics class and a dataset, upload the campaign export with Map CSV to XDM schema, create the lookup dataset, add both to the connection with the event data, set up the summary data group in the data view, then report spend and impressions next to site conversions.
routes.prerequisites: Included with CJA. Summary datasets carry no person ID and support hourly or daily granularity only.
routes.url_title: Use summary data (Customer Journey Analytics Guide)
routes.quote: showing summary data for running campaigns on Facebook
routes.notes: Create connection page: 'Summary data represents aggregated data at a different level of aggregation, for example campaigns.' and 'Only hourly or daily granularity is supported.' Works with an export from any ad platform; the API connectors are the next item.

routes.partner_work: Authorize each ad account (OAuth sign-in; Google Ads (V2) also needs a developer token and, for manager accounts, the login customer ID), select the ad accounts, let Experience Platform provision the paid media datasets and schedule, add them to a CJA connection and data view, and map tracking keys so ad data lines up with site conversions. For clients with Content Analytics, its paid media channel sets up the datasets and data view components automatically.

The Content Analytics paid media channel needs Content Analytics (licensed standalone since February 2026) and is not available on AWS-hosted deployments.
routes.quote: The Google Ads source is available as part of the Customer Journey Analytics SKU.
routes.notes: Pinterest page: 'The Pinterest Ads source is available as part of the Customer Journey Analytics SKU.' (same line on the Snapchat and TikTok pages). cja.summary:
Customer Journey Analytics never reads outside systems directly. Every route lands in an Experience Platform dataset first, and CJA reads that dataset through a connection and data view. Adobe's ingestion overview says: 'In all scenarios, the data you want to use in Customer Journey Analytics is actually ingested in Adobe Experience Platform.'

What a CJA license already covers:
- The Experience Platform pieces the data needs: data ingestion tools, the Data Lake, one Data Landing Zone per sandbox and up to 5 sandboxes.
- Non-Adobe sources: the product description says 'Customer may configure non-Adobe sources into Customer Journey Analytics (through UI and API).' That covers about 70 non-advanced connectors in Adobe's catalog (cloud storage, databases, CRM, customer service, marketing automation, e-commerce, payments, loyalty, consent, data partners, other analytics tools, generic REST and OData).
- The HTTP API streaming endpoint, CSV batch uploads, and the Edge Network (Web SDK, Mobile SDK, Server API) for websites, apps and devices.

Three limits matter for the canvas:
1. The warehouse and cloud streaming connectors (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, Synapse, Kinesis, Event Hubs, PubSub) are advanced enterprise sources. A CJA license may use them only through Data Mirror or with a separate license (Real-Time CDP Ultimate or the standalone Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors SKU).
2. Data Mirror (change data capture from Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks into relational datasets) needs CJA Select or higher. Adobe's pages disagree on its status: the CJA release notes give general availability on June 17 2026, while the Experience Platform page (Oct 21 2026) calls it a limited release.
3. CJA Foundation allows one event dataset per connection, so an outside event source next to web data needs Select or higher.

CJA dataset types drive the partner work: event, profile, lookup (classifications), summary (aggregates such as ad spend), ad hoc (CSV without schema design) and relational (Data Mirror).

Outside tools Adobe documents specifically for CJA:
- Google Analytics: history goes through a BigQuery export to Google Cloud Storage, live data through Tags with the Google Data Layer extension.
- Ad platforms: Google Ads (V2), Pinterest, Snapchat and TikTok sources are 'available as part of the Customer Journey Analytics SKU', and Meta Ads also feeds CJA.
- B2B Edition (add-on): adds account-based connections over account, opportunity, buying group and CRM datasets, with no Real-Time CDP B2B license needed for the standard schemas.
- Conversation Insights (Limited Testing): takes chatbot and call center transcripts as experience events.

Nothing is queried in place.

Outbound routes Adobe documents:
- Full table export to S3, Google Cloud, Azure, Snowflake and the Data Landing Zone.
- Dataset export to S3, Azure Blob, ADLS Gen2, Google Cloud Storage, SFTP and the Data Landing Zone.
- The BI extension for Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Jupyter and RStudio (Select or higher).
- Report Builder in Excel, MCP servers for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor, the Microsoft 365 Copilot agent, and the CJA APIs.

Fit with today's catalog: CJ01 (data preparation) and CJ03 (Analytics upgrade) cover ingestion only in general, so outside pieces would need lines per source. Adobe publishes no hours for any of this work.

The report's Server API item covers devices in general but not media tracking.

routes.mechanism: Experience Platform source connector, scheduled batch dataflow (Sources UI or Flow Service API)
routes.partner_work: Create read access on the client storage (S3: an IAM user with s3:GetObject and listing permissions, or temporary session credentials; Azure Blob: account key, SAS URI or service principal; Google Cloud Storage: an interoperability access key), add Adobe region IP ranges to the client allowlist, connect the account in Sources, pick the folder or file and its format (delimited, XDM JSON, XDM Parquet, compressed), choose or create the dataset and XDM schema, map fields with Data Prep, turn on Profile, error diagnostics, partial ingestion and alerts, set the schedule (once, or every 15 minutes up to weekly, with optional backfill), then check the first runs in the monitoring dashboard.
routes.prerequisites: View Sources and Manage Sources permissions (Admin Console); credentials for the client storage; region-specific IP allowlisting; FTP and Apache HDFS are beta connectors.
routes.quote: Cloud storage sources can bring your own data into Experience Platform without the need to download, format, or upload.
routes.notes: Azure Blob does not support same-region connectivity to Experience Platform. Batch sources such as Azure Blob, Amazon S3 and SFTP can ingest up to 200 GB per hour to the data lake (ingestion guardrails). Source dataflows that fail continuously for 30 days are disabled automatically. Change data capture into relational schemas is documented for S3, Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage and SFTP (see the Data Mirror item). Setup pages: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/connectors/cloud-storage/s3 and https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/ui-tutorials/dataflow/cloud-storage and https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/ingestion/guardrails

routes.mechanism: Client pushes files to an Adobe-provisioned Azure Blob container with SAS credentials, then a batch source dataflow ingests them
routes.partner_work: Retrieve the container SAS credentials from Experience Platform, set up the client job or tool that writes files there (Azure Storage Explorer, a command line, or an Azure Data Factory linked service), then build the same dataflow as any cloud storage source (format, dataset and schema, mapping, schedule, alerts), timing drops around the seven-day file expiry.
routes.prerequisites: Provisioned for every Experience Platform customer, one container per sandbox; total volume is limited by the Experience Platform license; no allowlist or network change needed (SAS over the public internet).
routes.quote: Data Landing Zone is an Azure Blob storage interface provisioned by Adobe Experience Platform
routes.notes: The page says Experience Platform deletes all files and folders seven days after upload. Change data capture is documented for Data Landing Zone, and Journey Optimizer orchestrated campaigns list it among supported sources. Useful when a client cannot open its own storage to Adobe IPs.

routes.mechanism: Advanced enterprise source connector, scheduled batch dataflow with incremental loads
routes.partner_work: Gather warehouse credentials (Snowflake key-pair authentication with account, username, private key, database and warehouse; BigQuery basic OAuth or a service account key; Databricks workspace domain, interactive cluster ID, access token and database, plus pasting the Adobe staging SAS URI into Databricks; Redshift and Synapse connection details), allowlist Adobe IP ranges, set the warehouse flags Adobe calls out (Snowflake PREVENT_UNLOAD_TO_INLINE_URL set to FALSE, UTC timestamps), select tables, choose dataset and schema, map with Data Prep, schedule with a UTC delta column for incremental loads and optional backfill, and subscribe to alerts.
routes.prerequisites: Real-Time CDP Ultimate, or the standalone Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors SKU; Manage Sources permission; warehouse credentials; IP allowlisting.
routes.quote: The following sources are only available to Adobe Real-Time Customer Data Platform Ultimate or customers who have licensed the standalone Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors SKU.
routes.notes: Table-based batch sources must use UTC; for Snowflake the only supported time stamp is TIMESTAMP_NTZ in UTC, and Snowflake reads null as an empty string unless Adobe changes it. This copies data into Experience Platform (compare Federated Audience Composition, which queries in place). Setup pages: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/ui-tutorials/create/databases/snowflake and https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/ui-tutorials/create/databases/bigquery and https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/ui-tutorials/create/databases/databricks and https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/ui-tutorials/dataflow/databases

routes.mechanism: Advanced enterprise streaming source connector, streaming dataflow
routes.partner_work: Provide stream credentials (Kinesis access key ID, secret access key and region; Event Hubs SAS key or Microsoft Entra ID app credentials; a Google service account for PubSub), create an Event Hubs consumer group first, select the stream, upload a sample JSON file for the schema, map to an XDM dataset and name the dataflow (an XDM-compliant stream can skip the sample). Adobe documents the Snowflake streaming source as available in the API.
routes.prerequisites: Real-Time CDP Ultimate (the Kinesis, Event Hubs, PubSub and Snowflake streaming pages each say so; the overview also allows the Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors SKU); stream credentials.
routes.url_title: Create a streaming dataflow for a cloud storage source in the UI
routes.quote: You can only create one source dataflow per consumer group for a given Event Hub.
routes.notes: Event Hubs ingests up to 2000 records per second unless Adobe scales it. Streaming sources are not shown in the sources monitoring dashboard. Kinesis page: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/connectors/cloud-storage/kinesis ; Snowflake streaming page: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/connectors/databases/snowflake-streaming ; Event Hubs auth: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/ui-tutorials/create/cloud-storage/eventhub

routes.mechanism: Adobe stream connector built on Kafka Connect (one-way sink) posting to an Experience Platform streaming HTTP endpoint
routes.partner_work: Download the connector library, add it to the client Kafka deployment, configure the topics to the Adobe streaming HTTP URL (an HTTP API streaming connection), and use authenticated collection and batching.
routes.prerequisites: A Kafka deployment run by the client; an HTTP API streaming connection in Experience Platform.
routes.quote: The stream connector for Adobe Experience Platform is based on Apache Kafka Connect.
routes.notes: Not a sources catalog card: it is a library the client runs. Ingestion guardrails say streaming sources such as Kafka, Azure Event Hubs and Amazon Kinesis do not use the Data Collection Core Service route and can have different throughput limits.

routes.mechanism: Database source connector, scheduled batch dataflow
routes.partner_work: Allowlist Adobe IP ranges on the client database network, create a read account and connection details, connect the source, browse tables and preview up to 100 rows, choose dataset and XDM schema, map with Data Prep, enable Profile and error diagnostics, schedule runs (minute intervals start at 15) with a UTC column for incremental loads and optional backfill, and subscribe to alerts.
routes.prerequisites: View and Manage Sources permissions; database credentials; IP allowlisting; four of these connectors are beta.
routes.url_title: Create a dataflow using a database source in the UI
routes.quote: A dataflow is a scheduled task that retrieves and ingests data from a source to a dataset in Adobe Experience Platform.
routes.notes: The page says timezones for all table-based batch sources must be configured to UTC. The sources overview groups these under Database: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/home

routes.mechanism: CRM source connector, scheduled batch dataflow (beta templates for Salesforce and Microsoft Dynamics)

routes.prerequisites: View and Manage Sources permissions; CRM admin access to create the connected app; Salesforce basic authentication is deprecated.
routes.url_title: Connect Salesforce to Experience Platform in the UI
routes.quote: The Salesforce source supports authentication via OAuth2 Client Credential.
routes.notes: The Salesforce source detects soft deletes only, not hard deletes. The change data capture page lists Salesforce and Microsoft Dynamics as supported. Overview line: "CRM systems provide data that can help build customer relationships, which in turn, create loyalty and drive customer retention." (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/home). Templates (beta): https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/ui-tutorials/templates

routes.mechanism: Protocol source connector, scheduled batch dataflow

routes.mechanism: HTTP API streaming source connection; Data Prep maps non-XDM JSON
routes.partner_work: Create the HTTP API connection, turn on authentication when PII is sent, mark it XDM compatible or raw, upload a sample payload, map to a dataset, build the client sender against the endpoint, allow the five-minute pause after creating or updating the dataflow, and size traffic to the streaming guidance (1000 requests per second).
routes.prerequisites: Manage Sources permission; streaming guardrails are bound to the organization license entitlement.
routes.quote: You can use the HTTP API source connector to stream your data to Experience Platform.
routes.notes: Streaming ingestion overview: Profile latency under 15 minutes at the 95th percentile for B2C, under 60 minutes to the data lake (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/ingestion/streaming/overview). Streaming sources are not in the sources monitoring dashboard. This is also the endpoint behind Journey Optimizer events.

routes.mechanism: Web or Mobile SDK, or the Edge Network API, sending to a datastream on the Adobe Edge Network
routes.partner_work: Implement the SDK (or the tags extension) on the client site or app, configure a datastream that sends to Experience Platform, design the XDM event schema, and validate that events reach the dataset and profile.

routes.quote: If none of the above SDKs accommodate your project’s needs, you can use the Adobe Experience Platform Edge Network API to send data directly to Adobe.

routes.mechanism: Local file upload source (one-off batch upload in the UI)

routes.quote: You can use the following sources to ingest data and identity partner data to Experience Platform.
routes.notes: Acxiom page: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/connectors/data-partner/acxiom-data-ingestion ; Demandbase page: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/connectors/data-partner/demandbase-b2b

routes.quote: You can use the following sources to ingest e-commerce data to Experience Platform.

(https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/connectors/ecommerce/shopify-streaming). routes.partner_work: Authenticate the platform (or point its event stream, such as Braze Currents, at the Adobe endpoint), map engagement data to XDM, schedule or stream, and monitor.
routes.prerequisites: View and Manage Sources permissions; platform credentials.
routes.quote: You can use the following sources to ingest marketing automation data to Experience Platform.
routes.notes: Braze Currents needs a Braze dashboard login, an unused Currents Connector license and permission to create a connector (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/connectors/marketing-automation/braze). Marketo Engage is listed under Adobe applications and is already on the canvas.

routes.mechanism: Sources SDK: build, test and submit a new connection specification through the Flow Service API

routes.quote: The Adobe Experience Platform Batch Ingestion API allows you to ingest data into Experience Platform as batch files.
routes.notes: Guardrails: up to 20 GB per hour to the data lake through the batch ingestion API (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/ingestion/guardrails).

routes.url_title: Create and manage connections with federated databases
routes.quote: Experience Platform Federated Audience Composition lets you build and enrich audiences from the third-party data warehouses and import the audiences to Adobe Experience Platform.
routes.notes: Adobe lists differ: the connections page names nine (adds Oracle and Teradata), the prerequisites page seven (no Oracle or Teradata), the FAQ eight (no Teradata). The FAQ says only metadata is stored and externally generated audiences expire after 30 days by default. The Adobe FAC architecture tutorial speaks of "a zero-copy pattern where Adobe Experience Platform becomes the engagement engine" (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/platform-learn/engage-with-audiences-from-your-data-warehouse-using-fac/fac-architecture-and-flow), and an Experience League Perspectives article calls it "a zero-copy query pattern" (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/perspectives/composable-by-design). The prerequisites page says Real-Time CDP and/or Journey Optimizer; the FAQ says Real-Time CDP and Journey Optimizer. platform.summary: Real-Time CDP and Journey Optimizer share one front door for outside data: Experience Platform. The sources overview (updated Oct 21, 2026) lists 79 non-Adobe connector entries in 16 categories: cloud storage, databases, advanced enterprise warehouses and event streams, CRM, customer success, payments, protocols, HTTP streaming, local upload, advertising, analytics, consent, data and identity partners, e-commerce, loyalty and marketing automation. Around the catalog sit the Batch Ingestion API, a Kafka Connect library, the Web and Mobile SDKs and Edge Network API, CSV audience import, prospect profiles from data partners, and a Sources SDK for systems that are not listed. Journey Optimizer's own pages say it uses the same sources framework and keeps no separate data store, so every connector above reaches it too. The partner work Adobe documents is the same everywhere: credentials and an allowlist of Adobe's region IPs, select the data, map to XDM with Data Prep, schedule (once, or every 15 minutes up to weekly, with backfill and a UTC incremental column), then alerts and monitoring (the dashboard covers batch only; dataflows failing 30 days are disabled). Adobe publishes no hours. For data warehouses there are three documented patterns. Copy: Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks and Synapse source connectors, plus Kinesis, Event Hubs, PubSub and Snowflake streaming, all gated to Real-Time CDP Ultimate or the standalone Advanced Enterprise Source Connectors SKU. Mirror: Data Mirror with change data capture into relational schemas (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks and file sources), required for Journey Optimizer orchestrated campaigns; Adobe's availability statements conflict. Query in place: Federated Audience Composition, an add-on to Real-Time CDP and/or Journey Optimizer Prime or Ultimate, nine warehouses on its connections page, audiences usable in Read Audience journeys. Adobe uses the term zero-copy for the outbound Delta Sharing destinations to Databricks and Snowflake (Beta, Ultimate) and, in a tutorial and a Perspectives article, for the Federated Audience Composition pattern. Journey Optimizer adds routes that leave data where it is: external data sources and custom actions call any REST and JSON API during a journey (Adobe now prefers custom actions with responses), and Integrations pull content and data at send time from systems such as Contentful, Sitecore, Salsify, Talon.One or Databricks. Outside systems trigger journeys by posting events to Experience Platform streaming endpoints; batch events cannot. Out of Adobe, briefly: cloud storage, Snowflake data share, HTTP API, ad and social destinations, dataset export, event forwarding, Query Service for BI tools, and SMS providers (Sinch, Twilio, Infobip). For the canvas, these routes group into a few outside boxes partners would recognize (data warehouse, cloud storage, CRM, event streams, website and apps, third-party APIs, ad platforms), each with its own license gate and documented steps, where today's catalog folds all of it into one generic line per product (RT02 Data sources and ingestion setup, JO02 Journey events, data sources and actions). Discrepancies to keep in mind: Federated Audience Composition's supported list (7, 8 or 9 systems by page), its package wording (and/or versus and), Data Mirror availability, and the change data capture source list. business.adobe.com pages returned errors during this research, so nothing here relies on them; every quote was checked against the downloaded Experience League page.

routes.mechanism: Checkout starter kit tax app with the out-of-process tax management module; an outside tax service drives quote tax calculation
routes.partner_work: Register the tax integration (only one can be active), build the tax calculation action, set up the Tax Management admin UI, and test quotes and orders; check for conflicts with any installed tax extension first.
routes.prerequisites: Commerce as a Cloud Service, or Commerce on cloud or on-premises 2.4.5 and later; App Builder.
routes.quote: To enable out-of-process tax management in Adobe Commerce, install the magento/module-out-of-process-tax-management module
routes.notes: Same page: "this extension is not compatible with other tax extensions that also override this class, such as TaxJar or Avalara." Uninstalling returns tax calculation to Commerce.

routes.mechanism: Built-in carrier integrations set up in the Admin with the merchant's own carrier account and the carrier's gateway URL; rates come back automatically and labels can be printed
routes.partner_work: Set the store's point of origin, collect each carrier account, enter account numbers or user IDs and gateway URLs per carrier, set up shipping labels where needed, and move USPS to the REST APIs (quality patch or upgrade).
routes.prerequisites: A commercial account with each carrier; USPS needs the REST API configuration because the Legacy Web Tools APIs were retired on January 25, 2026.
routes.quote: Enter your account number or user ID, and the gateway URL to their system into the configuration of your store.
routes.notes: The page points to the Commerce Marketplace for more shipping services ("See Commerce Marketplace for additional shipping services for your Commerce installation").

routes.mechanism: Native and bundled payment integrations configured in the Admin; Amazon Pay, Klarna and other gateways come as Commerce Marketplace extensions
routes.partner_work: Choose the payment methods, set up the merchant accounts and credentials, configure each method in the Admin, test in sandbox, and review the PCI compliance guidelines.
routes.prerequisites: A merchant account with each provider; PayPal Express Checkout, Braintree and the other PayPal solutions are marked PaaS only; from 2.4.4, Amazon Pay and Klarna are installed from the Commerce Marketplace.
routes.quote: There are also native integrations for numerous online payment solutions and gateways, including Braintree as a bundled vendor-developed extension.
routes.notes: Payment Services is Adobe's own payment service and the default on Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service; it offers card fields, digital wallets and "PayPal products and services" (Introduction to Payment Services).

routes.mechanism: Fraud filters and fraud protection extensions from the Commerce Marketplace that screen orders before the transaction is processed
routes.partner_work: Choose the fraud solution, install the extension from the Marketplace where it is not native, configure the filters, and test order flows.
routes.prerequisites: Marked PaaS only on the page; an account with the fraud provider.
routes.quote: Fraud protection services and filters examine submitted orders before the transaction is processed to detect fraudulent orders
routes.notes: Signifyd was removed from the core release in 2.4.0; the page recommends the vendor's Signifyd Fraud and Chargeback Protection extension.

routes.mechanism: Tax calculation extension installed from the Commerce Marketplace and selected as the tax calculation method in the Admin
routes.partner_work: Install the Vertex extension from the Marketplace or the vendor, connect the Vertex account, select the extension service in the tax settings, and test tax on quotes and orders.
routes.prerequisites: A Vertex account; from 2.4.4 the extension is no longer bundled and must be installed from the Commerce Marketplace.
routes.quote: If a tax calculation extension is installed from the Marketplace, such as Vertex Cloud
routes.notes: The Taxes page adds that the Vertex extension provided "tax management and address cleansing" and to contact Vertex for documentation.

routes.category: Any third-party API (OMS, ERP inventory, logistics, pricing engine)
routes.mechanism: API Mesh for Adobe Developer App Builder: one managed GraphQL endpoint that combines Commerce GraphQL, REST (OpenAPI) and JSON Schema sources at query time
routes.partner_work: Write mesh.json with each source and its handler (graphql, openapi, JsonSchema), keep credentials in App Builder environment variables, add custom resolvers with batching where needed, decide on caching (native, or a CDN in front of the mesh), and deploy with the aio CLI.
routes.prerequisites: App Builder access (the mesh is configured and deployed with the aio CLI in an App Builder workspace); the outside APIs and their credentials.
routes.url_title: API Mesh for Adobe Developer App Builder
routes.quote: an orchestration layer that enables developers to seamlessly integrate private and third-party APIs with Adobe products and APIs
routes.notes: Adobe's Commerce article (experienceleague.adobe.com/en/perspectives/api-mesh-on-adobe-commerce-a-unified-graphql-graph-for-headless-storefronts) names the openapi handler for "third-party OMS (Order Management System) REST APIs" and shows one mesh combining Commerce, Catalog Service and an OMS. API Mesh is for synchronous query-time federation, not event-driven integration.

routes.category: PIM, ERP or third-party commerce engine (catalog source)
routes.mechanism: Adobe Commerce Optimizer Data Ingestion API (REST) loading product attribute metadata, categories, products, price books and prices from the source system
routes.partner_work: Define the product attribute metadata (sku, name, description, shortDescription and price for each catalog source), map and load categories, products and prices, set up catalog views and policies, and watch Data Sync.
routes.prerequisites: Adobe Commerce Optimizer (SaaS only; Adobe points to its Limits and boundaries topic for licensing); IMS credentials for the API.
routes.quote: Ingest catalog data from any third-party source (your existing Commerce catalog, PIM, ERP, and so on).
routes.notes: The Data Ingestion API "is designed to be used by backend applications to manage product data" (developer.adobe.com/commerce/services/optimizer/data-ingestion/). Optimizer is for merchants "who want to maintain their existing backend commerce system". Adobe Commerce Optimizer is a separate Commerce offering, not Adobe Commerce itself.

routes.mechanism: Adobe Commerce Optimizer storefront calling a third-party cart and checkout through API Mesh and App Builder
routes.partner_work: Build the API Mesh and App Builder integration between the Edge Delivery storefront and the outside cart and checkout, then test the shopping flow end to end.
routes.prerequisites: Adobe Commerce Optimizer; App Builder access.
routes.quote: Use API mesh and App builder to integrate with third-party cart and checkout systems.
routes.notes: Adobe lists "Businesses where a third-party system manages the cart and checkout lifecycle" among Optimizer's audience.

routes.category: CRM, ERP, CMS and other applications (API clients)
routes.mechanism: Commerce web APIs (REST, GraphQL, SOAP) called by a third-party application registered as an Admin integration with OAuth 1.0a on PaaS (IMS OAuth server-to-server credentials on Commerce as a Cloud Service)
routes.partner_work: Create and authorize the integration with only the API resources it needs, set the callback and identity link URLs, store the tokens, and build and test the API calls on the outside system.
routes.prerequisites: Admin access to System > Extensions > Integrations (PaaS); IMS credentials on Commerce as a Cloud Service.
routes.url_title: Getting started with Adobe Commerce web APIs
routes.quote: Integrate with CRM (Customer Relationship Management) or ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) backend systems, such as Salesforce or Xero.
routes.notes: The Admin Integrations page (PaaS only) says an integration "establishes the location of OAuth credentials and redirect URL for third-party integrations" (experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-admin/systems/integrations). The same web API page also lists integrating with a CMS.

routes.category: File transfer (FTP) for product and customer feeds
routes.mechanism: Scheduled Import/Export jobs (CSV) that read from or write to a remote FTP server daily, weekly or monthly, run by cron
routes.partner_work: Set up each job (entity type, import behavior, Remote FTP server type, credentials, path, file name, schedule), map the CSV layout from the source system, and watch the failure emails and the Last Outcome column.
routes.prerequisites: Adobe Commerce (not Magento Open Source); cron running; an FTP server Commerce can reach.
routes.quote: The files to be imported or exported can reside on local Adobe Commerce servers, or on remote FTP servers.
routes.notes: Scheduled imports cover product and customer data in CSV. The page names FTP; SFTP is not mentioned.

routes.mechanism: Remote Storage module keeping media files and import/export files in an AWS S3 bucket
routes.partner_work: Set the remote storage driver, bucket and region with the setup CLI, move the media, and check custom code for file functions the module does not allow.
routes.prerequisites: Commerce 2.4.2 or later; an AWS S3 bucket; database media storage turned off; limited support on Commerce on cloud infrastructure.
routes.quote: provides the option to store media files and schedule imports and exports in a persistent, remote storage container
routes.notes: The driver value aws-s3 means "Use the Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)". Adobe: "Adobe cannot fully troubleshoot the third-party storage adapter service."

routes.mechanism: Fastly CDN, WAF and related services provided with Adobe Commerce on cloud infrastructure, managed from the Commerce Admin with per-environment Fastly credentials
routes.partner_work: Set up Fastly on Staging and Production, add custom VCL snippets, configure routing (including Edge Delivery storefront paths), and validate caching and the WAF.
routes.prerequisites: Adobe Commerce on cloud infrastructure; the Fastly service account is Adobe's, and each Staging and Production environment gets its own Fastly API token and service ID.
routes.quote: Fastly provides the following services to optimize and secure content delivery operations for Adobe Commerce on cloud infrastructure projects.
routes.notes: Adobe warns that Fastly must be set up on Starter main, Pro Production and Pro Staging to keep PCI compliance. Customers do not get Fastly dashboard access.

routes.category: CDN (bring your own) for the Commerce storefront
routes.mechanism: Commerce storefront on Edge Delivery Services served through the customer's own CDN (BYO CDN) instead of the default Fastly (Commerce on Cloud) or Adobe-managed CDN (Commerce as a Cloud Service)
routes.partner_work: Configure routing between Edge Delivery Services and Commerce paths (Admin and GraphQL to Commerce), image optimization parameters, push invalidation, and validation.
routes.prerequisites: A Commerce storefront on Edge Delivery Services; the customer's CDN account.
routes.quote: If necessary, you can configure your own CDN
routes.notes: Vendor-specific BYO CDN steps are on the linked BYO CDN Setup page (Edge Delivery Services docs), so the vendor list belongs with the Edge Delivery Services research.

routes.mechanism: New Relic log management, APM and Infrastructure included and pre-configured on Adobe Commerce on cloud infrastructure
routes.partner_work: Build New Relic queries, dashboards and alerts over application, cloud service, Fastly CDN and WAF logs, and use them to troubleshoot.
routes.prerequisites: Adobe Commerce on cloud infrastructure; access to the project's New Relic account.
routes.quote: All cloud infrastructure projects include New Relic log management.
routes.notes: The log data covers application logs, cloud service logs and Fastly CDN and WAF logs.

routes.mechanism: OpenTelemetry instrumentation of eventing, webhooks, App Builder apps and the starter kits, with the out-of-process Observability module routing telemetry to OTLP endpoints
routes.partner_work: Instrument the App Builder apps and starter kits with OpenTelemetry, subscribe the OTLP endpoints, and build cross-service traces, dashboards and alerts in the chosen tool.
routes.prerequisites: Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service, or PaaS with App Builder apps; an observability backend that accepts OpenTelemetry data.
routes.quote: send their metrics, logs, and traces to popular services such as New Relic, Splunk, Prometheus, Datadog
routes.notes: The out-of-process modules page says the Observability module "manages subscriptions for the location where logs, metrics, and traces are routed (OTLP endpoints)."

routes.mechanism: Catalog search engine every Commerce 2.4 installation on-premises or on cloud infrastructure must run, unless Live Search (Adobe SaaS) takes over storefront search
routes.partner_work: Install and size OpenSearch, put it behind a web server proxy with TLS and HTTP Basic authentication, connect Commerce, and plan any move to Live Search (the two cannot share storefront search).
routes.prerequisites: Adobe Commerce 2.4 on-premises or on cloud infrastructure; OpenSearch is supported from 2.4.4.
routes.quote: As of Adobe Commerce 2.4, all installations must be configured to use Elasticsearch or OpenSearch as the catalog search solution.
routes.notes: Experience League KB ka-26926: "Live Search and OpenSearch cannot be used concurrently for storefront catalog search functionality." Third-party site search vendors are not documented beyond Marketplace extensions.

routes.mechanism: Adobe Commerce Intelligence database integrations (SSH tunnel recommended) that sync tables into the Commerce Intelligence Data Warehouse
routes.partner_work: Set up the SSH tunnel or credentials, restrict database access, choose the tables to sync in the Data Warehouse Manager, and consolidate tables for reporting.
routes.prerequisites: An Adobe Commerce Intelligence account; database access.
routes.quote: Commerce Intelligence supports SQL-based and NoSQL databases such as MySQL, Microsoft SQL, MongoDB, and PostgreSQL.
routes.notes: Adobe Commerce Intelligence was previously Magento Business Intelligence; it is its own product with its own account.

routes.category: SaaS apps (CRM, ads, support, web analytics) for reporting
routes.mechanism: Adobe Commerce Intelligence SaaS integrations authorized with account credentials or API keys
routes.partner_work: Generate the credentials, add each integration under Manage Data > Connections, pick tables in the Data Warehouse Manager, and join them with Commerce data in reports.
routes.prerequisites: An Adobe Commerce Intelligence account; vendor credentials or API keys; some integrations must be activated by support before they appear.
routes.quote: SaaS integrations are services like Google Adwords, Salesforce, and Zendesk.
routes.notes: Google Analytics appears among the connection types on the same page.

routes.category: Files and custom sources for reporting
routes.mechanism: Adobe Commerce Intelligence File Upload (.csv) and the Commerce Intelligence Import API
routes.partner_work: Format and upload CSV files, or write and maintain a small script against the Import API, then join the data with other sources in the Data Warehouse.
routes.prerequisites: An Adobe Commerce Intelligence account; an API key for the Import API.
routes.quote: you can quickly upload .csv files into your Data Warehouse and join them with other data sources
routes.notes: Same page: "if it is not in a database or a SaaS integration, the Import API function is your best bet."

routes.category: Third-party extensions (connectors for ERP, PIM, payments, shipping, tax, search)
routes.mechanism: Commerce Marketplace extensions installed with Composer as in-process modules (on-premises and cloud infrastructure)
routes.partner_work: Vet the extension, add the repo.magento.com repository, install with Composer, enable and configure the module, keep it updated, and get removal steps from the vendor.
routes.prerequisites: The Marketplace purchase and the Marketplace authentication keys; a PaaS project (on-premises or cloud infrastructure).
routes.quote: manage third-party extensions that you purchase from the Commerce Marketplace
routes.notes: The shipping, payments and tax pages all point to the Marketplace for more providers. For new work Adobe recommends out-of-process App Builder apps over in-process modules.

routes.mechanism: Out-of-process App Builder app on the App Management lifecycle, connected to Commerce through APIs, events, webhooks and Admin UI extension points
routes.partner_work: Define the app, build it on App Builder with the Commerce SDKs, connect it through APIs, events or webhooks, deploy and associate it with the Commerce instance through App Management, and operate it with observability.
routes.prerequisites: App Builder access; Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service, or Commerce on cloud or on-premises.
routes.url_title: Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service overview
routes.quote: integrate with third-party systems (such as CRMs, ERPs, and PIMs)
routes.notes: The Commerce extensibility home page (developer.adobe.com/commerce/extensibility/) says custom business logic and integrations "run as applications outside the Commerce application process."

routes.category: Experience Platform (Adobe hop toward outside destinations)
routes.mechanism: Data Connection extension sending storefront events, back office events and profile records to the Experience Platform Edge Network; Audience Activation brings Real-Time CDP audiences back
routes.partner_work: Already scoped on the canvas as commerce-rtcdp (XA14 Data Connection, XA15 Audience Activation): Commerce Services connector, schemas, datasets, datastream, and storefront, back office and profile data.
routes.prerequisites: Experience Platform; Real-Time CDP for Audience Activation (PaaS only).
routes.quote: The Data Connection extension connects your Adobe Commerce web instance to the Adobe Experience Platform and the Edge Network.
routes.notes: Not an outside route by itself. It is how Commerce data reaches Experience Platform; sending it on to a data warehouse or other outside system would use Experience Platform destinations, which the Commerce pages do not describe.

routes.category: Website content on any platform or CMS
routes.mechanism: Website Links knowledge source: crawl of a sitemap, individual URLs or a CSV of URLs, with an optional scheduled refresh
routes.partner_work: Choose the sitemap or URL list (or fill the CSV template), schedule refreshes, check processing status, download the Fix Issues report, correct or remove failed URLs, and reprocess.
routes.prerequisites: Brand Concierge in an Experience Platform sandbox; publicly crawlable pages.
routes.url_title: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge
routes.quote: Crawls a sitemap, selected individual URLs, or URLs supplied in a CSV file.
routes.notes: Same page: "This option works for websites built on any platform and is the recommended option for most first-time users." A concierge answers only from its configured knowledge sources.

routes.category: Product catalog from a non-Adobe commerce system or PIM export
routes.mechanism: Product Catalog knowledge source: a spreadsheet uploaded against a schema (custom product schemas supported) that drives product cards and deep links
routes.partner_work: Pick or define the schema (fields, buttons, links), export the client's product data into the sample spreadsheet, upload it, and test the product cards and links.
routes.prerequisites: Brand Concierge; a small catalog (about fewer than 100 products or services) that is not on Adobe Commerce.
routes.url_title: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge
routes.quote: The customer has a relatively small product or service catalog and is not using Adobe Commerce.
routes.notes: February 2026 release notes: custom product schema support lets customers "upload and manage product catalogs that follow their own data structure rather than a fixed format." A live feed from a non-Adobe commerce engine is not documented; large Adobe Commerce catalogs use Adobe's Commerce MCP integration.

routes.mechanism: Upload of PDF and DOCX files as concierge knowledge
routes.partner_work: Collect the approved documents, clean them up, upload them, and check answers against them in evaluation.
routes.prerequisites: Brand Concierge.
routes.quote: In addition, Brand Concierge now supports PDF/DOCX file upload.
routes.notes: The go-live guide lists "website URLs, PDFs, and product spreadsheets" as the three knowledge source types, but the October 2 2026 knowledge sources page lists AEM Sites, Website Links and Product Catalog and gives no file upload steps.

routes.category: Third-party APIs, inventory systems and outside knowledge bases
routes.mechanism: A new integration in the Skills and Integrations Framework that skills call at runtime; none exists in the out-of-the-box catalog, so it has to be built first
routes.partner_work: Per the docs, attaching, configuring and instructing an existing integration is self-serve; building a connector that is not in the catalog is an engineering task, and the docs do not say who does it.
routes.prerequisites: An integration for the outside system in the catalog.
routes.quote: Create a brand-new tool or connector that does not already exist in the catalog
routes.notes: The FAQ lists "Inventory systems", "Knowledge bases and documentation" and "Third-party APIs (configured)" as data sources, but the out-of-the-box integrations are Knowledge Base Search, Content AI Search, Entity Linking, Commerce MCP, Meeting Booking and Live Chat, all Adobe.

routes.category: Website on a non-Adobe CMS or platform (delivery)
routes.mechanism: Experience Platform Web SDK plus the Brand Concierge Web Client script, added through a tag manager or in code, with surface rules for pages and domains
routes.partner_work: Instrument the site with the Web SDK and a datastream enabled for Brand Concierge, add the Web Client script and bootstrap call, set surface rules, style the widget, and test on desktop and mobile.
routes.prerequisites: The organization is an Experience Platform customer; the page runs the Experience Platform Web SDK; a datastream enabled for Brand Concierge.
routes.quote: The JavaScript SDK integrates with any website, and mobile SDKs work with any app backend.
routes.notes: Developer guide prerequisite: "The organization is an Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) customer." The FAQ also says the concierge is domain agnostic.

routes.mechanism: Brand Concierge extension for the Experience Platform Mobile SDK, with sendDataHandoff for passing XDM data from the host app
routes.partner_work: Install and register the extension, theme the chat UI, set the session XDM context, handle links with the handleLink callback, and test in the app.
routes.prerequisites: Experience Platform Mobile SDK with Configuration and Edge Identity.
routes.quote: an in-app conversational UI (a chat surface) that can be embedded into a host app with minimal UI wiring
routes.notes: Mobile SDK release notes: "Added Concierge.sendDataHandoff for sending XDM data through the Brand Concierge service."

routes.mechanism: Client-side onEvent callback registered in bootstrap(), observing lifecycle, interaction, response, feedback and error events
routes.partner_work: Write the onEvent handler, map event types to the analytics tool's events, send them without blocking the page (for example sendBeacon), forward errors to an error-tracking service, and test.
routes.prerequisites: The Brand Concierge Web Client on the page.
routes.quote: useful for sending engagement data to Adobe Analytics, Google Analytics, or other third-party systems
routes.notes: The callback is read-only and cannot change the client's behavior. Released in August 2026.

routes.mechanism: Experience Platform Query Service (SQL) over the Brand Concierge conversation datasets, run from the UI, the API or a connected client, with downloadable results
routes.partner_work: Find the cja_brand_concierge datasets and their table names in each sandbox, write the SQL, and set up the reporting pull (UI download, API or connected client).
routes.prerequisites: Experience Platform access to Queries and to the Brand Concierge datasets in the same sandbox.
routes.quote: Run the query from your organization’s Query Service workflow (UI, API, or connected client)
routes.notes: Which outside BI clients can connect to Query Service is covered on Experience Platform pages, not Brand Concierge pages.

routes.mechanism: Representatives connect Outlook or Google calendars in Adobe Marketo Qualifier; the Meeting Booking integration reads open slots and books meetings, optionally with a Microsoft Teams link
routes.partner_work: Add representatives in the Admin Console, have each connect a calendar and set availability, edit the confirmation email, choose routing, connect the Meeting Booking integration, and activate the Handoff to sales skill with its Use when conditions.
routes.prerequisites: Access to Adobe Marketo Qualifier; representatives added as users in the Adobe Admin Console; at least one connected calendar.
routes.url_title: Set up representatives in Adobe Marketo Qualifier
routes.quote: Choose the calendar you want to connect, either Microsoft Outlook or Google Calendar.
routes.notes: Same page: representatives "choose whether to include a Microsoft Teams meeting link in the invitation." Adobe Marketo Qualifier (formerly Sales Qualifier) is an Adobe companion product.

routes.mechanism: Concierge activities and the representative's conversation score written to Marketo Engage person records, then used in Smart Campaigns for handoff to the CRM through Marketo
routes.partner_work: Connect Marketo Engage (admin access and a feature flag), check the lead source fields, and build Smart Campaigns on the three concierge activity types, including conversation score, for lead scoring and CRM handoff.
routes.prerequisites: Adobe Marketo Engage connected to Brand Concierge.
routes.quote: Use it to drive retargeting, lead scoring, personalization, and CRM handoff.
routes.notes: Brand Concierge documents no direct CRM connector; the CRM step relies on Marketo Engage's own CRM sync, which belongs to the Marketo research.

routes.mechanism: Bring Your Own Agent through the Experience Platform Agent Orchestrator
routes.partner_work: Not documented: the release note announces the capability with Adobe's own Firefly agent on Adobe.com and gives no customer setup steps.
routes.prerequisites: Not documented.
routes.quote: enabling customer and third-party agents within Brand Concierge via the Agent Orchestrator
routes.notes: March 2026 release note, called the first launch of the Bring Your Own Agent integration.

routes.mechanism: Context-aware product recommendation that can integrate with the client's product search and recommendation systems of record
routes.partner_work: Not documented beyond the release note; the only live catalog integration in the out-of-the-box catalog is Adobe's Commerce MCP, backed by Live Search.
routes.prerequisites: Not documented.
routes.quote: the ability to integrate with product search and recommendation systems of record to improve relevance and accuracy
routes.notes: April 2026 release note; no setup page was found.

routes.mechanism: MCP connectors in Coworker Chat: out-of-the-box connectors plus bring-your-own, under Coworker's governance (approval gates, inherited permissions, audit trail)
routes.partner_work: Decide which client systems Coworker should reach, use an out-of-the-box connector where one exists or bring the client's own MCP server, and test each connection with real tasks under the client's approval gates and permissions.
routes.prerequisites: Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker licensed and enabled for the organization; roles assigned in the Admin Console.
routes.quote: governed access to act across Adobe and third-party systems, with out-of-the-box connectors and the option to bring your own
routes.notes: The public pages do not list the out-of-the-box connectors by name.

routes.category: Any outside tool or service (custom MCP server)
routes.mechanism: Connect a server under Customizations > User > Integrations: an MCP server endpoint over SSE or HTTP, with an authentication method, optional headers such as an API key, and a tool timeout
routes.partner_work: Stand up or pick the MCP server for each outside tool, add it (name, URL, connection type, authentication, headers, timeout), check the active connections, and point skills at it.
routes.prerequisites: Coworker Chat access; an MCP server endpoint and its credentials.
routes.quote: Enter a name that identifies the server in your list of integrations, for example github or slack.
routes.notes: GitHub and Slack appear only as example server names. The same section's examples of servers are Adobe apps ("Adobe Journey Optimizer, Real-Time CDP, Target, and Workfront"). The overview page says: "To connect Coworker Chat to an external tool or service, add it as a server under Customizations > User > Integrations."

routes.mechanism: An admin adds a marketplace from a GitHub repository; plugins from it bundle skills and MCP servers and are installed for the organization or by users
routes.partner_work: Package the client's skills and server connections as a plugin in a GitHub-hosted marketplace, have the admin add the marketplace, review the plugin's skills before deployment, and decide whether users may install or remove plugins.
routes.prerequisites: Coworker admin rights; a GitHub repository for the marketplace; a validated Experience Cloud organization and Experience Platform sandbox.
routes.quote: How to add a new marketplace using a GitHub repository
routes.notes: What are plugins? page: "Installing a plugin does not automatically grant access to products or actions that a user is not already authorized to use." Who builds plugins is not stated.

routes.mechanism: Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot (Coworker for AI Platforms), giving read-only insights under the user's Adobe permissions
routes.partner_work: Have the Microsoft 365 admin allow agents from external publishers, approve Coworker in the Microsoft 365 admin center and the Teams admin center, deploy it to users or groups, then train users with example prompts.
routes.prerequisites: Coworker provisioned with user access; Experience Platform plus at least one of Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer or Customer Journey Analytics; Microsoft 365 Copilot.
routes.url_title: Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker for AI Platforms
routes.quote: you can access it across Microsoft 365 Copilot surfaces, including Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and web chat
routes.notes: Same page: "Coworker returns read-only insights and does not modify your customer data." Known limitation: "You cannot connect Coworker to your own agentic harness using MCP."

routes.mechanism: Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker plugin in ChatGPT, approved by the ChatGPT administrator, giving read-only insights
routes.partner_work: Have the ChatGPT admin approve Coworker for selected users or the whole organization; users install it from the plugin catalog.
routes.prerequisites: Coworker provisioned with user access; Experience Platform plus at least one of Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer or Customer Journey Analytics; ChatGPT.
routes.url_title: Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker for AI Platforms
routes.quote: find and select Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker in the plugin catalog
routes.notes: Same read-only scope and permissions as the Copilot route.

routes.mechanism: Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker connector in Claude, approved by the Claude administrator and signed in with Adobe credentials, giving read-only insights
routes.partner_work: Have the Claude admin approve Coworker for selected users or the whole organization; users connect it from Connectors and sign in with Adobe credentials.
routes.prerequisites: Coworker provisioned with user access; Experience Platform plus at least one of Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer or Customer Journey Analytics; Claude.
routes.url_title: Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker for AI Platforms
routes.quote: Select Connectors, then Discover, and use Search to find Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker.
routes.notes: Same read-only scope and permissions as the Copilot route.

routes.category: Other enterprise systems (customer and account data)
routes.mechanism: Experience Context in the Coworker navigation rail
routes.partner_work: Not described beyond a one-line definition; no setup page was found.
routes.prerequisites: Not documented.
routes.quote: Connect Coworker to your existing Adobe applications (like Marketo Engage) and other enterprise systems
routes.notes: The mechanism (MCP server or something else) is not stated.

routes.mechanism: Attach a file for Coworker Chat to read; download table artifacts as CSV
routes.partner_work: Nothing to configure; cover file use in skills, prompts and training.
routes.prerequisites: Coworker Chat access.
routes.quote: Attach file: Upload a file for Coworker Chat to read and reference.
routes.notes: Same page: "You can download a table artifact as a CSV file from its card."

commerce-bc-cw.summary:
51 documented routes across the three products: 28 for Adobe Commerce, 12 for Brand Concierge, 11 for Coworker. Every quote, including the quotes inside notes, was checked word for word against Experience League and developer.adobe.com pages downloaded on Nov 2 2026. The items, the check script and the page copies are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warroom/432cd4fe-7682-5283-bb86-965652091bf2/scratchpad/outside/cbc/ (items_cbc.json, scripts/verify.py, pages/). business.adobe.com refused every request (HTTP 503), so nothing here rests on it.

Commerce is wide open to outside systems and is the natural home for optional outside pieces. Adobe documents generic routes rather than one per vendor. They include:
- the integration starter kit on App Builder: ERP, OMS and CRM, with customers, orders, products, shipments and stock flowing both ways
- I/O Events, delivered to App Builder, webhook URLs or Amazon EventBridge
- synchronous webhooks: stock, totals, tax and payment checks against an OMS or other service
- API Mesh: any REST, OpenAPI or GraphQL source, queried in place
- out-of-process payment, shipping and tax apps
- web APIs with OAuth integrations (Salesforce and Xero as examples)
- FTP scheduled import and export, and S3 remote storage
- the Commerce Optimizer Data Ingestion API: any PIM, ERP or commerce engine as a catalog source, plus third-party cart and checkout

Named vendors appear only for built-ins and Marketplace items: UPS, USPS, FedEx and DHL; Payment Services, PayPal, Braintree, Amazon Pay and Klarna; Vertex; Signifyd; Amazon S3; Fastly; New Relic, Splunk, Prometheus and Datadog; OpenSearch. Commerce Intelligence reporting adds MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Google AdWords, Salesforce, Zendesk and Google Analytics. The extensibility routes need App Builder access. Adobe supports only the starter kits' basic functionality, not modified code or custom integrations.

Brand Concierge is mostly closed.
- Outside content comes in three ways: crawling any website (sitemap, URLs or a CSV of URLs), a spreadsheet for small non-Adobe catalogs, and PDF or DOCX uploads.
- It runs on any website or app, but needs the Experience Platform Web or Mobile SDK. It can send client-side events to Google Analytics or other tools, and Query Service can pull conversation data out.
- Human handoff runs through Adobe Marketo Qualifier, with Outlook or Google calendars and Teams links. It reaches a CRM only through Marketo Engage.
- Every out-of-the-box integration is Adobe's. A connector for any outside API, inventory system or knowledge base is an engineering build that the docs leave unassigned. Handoff to an outside contact center is listed as upcoming.

Coworker is open by design through MCP.
- Any MCP server can be added (SSE or HTTP, with auth and headers).
- Plugins that bundle skills and servers install from marketplaces hosted on GitHub.
- Coworker also appears read-only inside Microsoft 365 Copilot (Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint), ChatGPT and Claude. That route needs Experience Platform plus Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer or CJA.
- The public docs name no specific third-party connector; Jira, Slack, Asana and SharePoint appear only in Adobe's internal deck.
- The separate Coworker for teams app has a HubSpot connector and names Databricks and Salesforce.

For the canvas, these fit Adam's idea of optional outside pieces:
- Commerce outside pieces map cleanly to documented partner work: back office integration, checkout extensions, API Mesh, catalog ingestion, CDN and observability.
- Coworker's map to 'connect an MCP server' and 'package a plugin'.
- Brand Concierge's are content and channel inputs, with handoff and CRM going through Adobe's Marketo products.

One Adobe to Adobe item, Commerce Data Connection to Experience Platform, is included because the task named it; it is already on the canvas as commerce-rtcdp.

routes.mechanism: BYOCDN log forwarding: the customer's CDN pushes its access logs to an Adobe-owned Amazon S3 bucket (Akamai DataStream to S3, Cloudflare Logpush, CloudFront standard logging or AWS CLI cross-account delivery, Fastly S3 logging endpoint, Imperva S3 ARN connection).
routes.partner_work: Onboard the CDN in Brand Visibility (Brands Management, CDN, Activate AI Traffic Insights) to get the bucket, path, region and keys. With the customer's CDN administrator, create the log job in the CDN console using the fields, format and push interval Brand Visibility shows (for example JSON, all logs and RFC3339 timestamps on Cloudflare; Adobe's log format string and Gzip on Fastly; the mapped DataStream fields on Akamai; the AWS account ID for CloudFront). Validate the destination test file, then confirm the Agentic Traffic and Referral Traffic dashboards fill. Fastly and Akamai S3 credentials can be rotated from Customer Configuration.
routes.prerequisites: Domain onboarded in Brand Visibility; a Brand Visibility user allowed to manage CDN configuration; admin access to the CDN console; for CloudFront, the AWS account ID and rights to set up cross-account log delivery. No add-on is named.

routes.quote: Without CDN log forwarding, the Agentic Traffic dashboard cannot display metrics.
routes.notes: Unlocks the Agentic Traffic dashboard, page hits on Referral Traffic and prompt suggestions from citation attempts. Quick Start: 'To unlock Agentic Traffic and Referral Traffic insights, register CDN log forwarding so Adobe Brand Visibility can read your access logs.' Adobe says no personal data is processed in CDN log ingestion. Already inside the catalog's L02 as customer IT work (the long pole). Backfills to earlier folders are picked up within 24 hours.

routes.mechanism: Optimize at Edge on a customer-managed CDN (BYOCDN): routing rules send AI-agent requests to Adobe's Edge Optimize backend (live.edgeoptimize.net), which returns optimized HTML; people and search bots still get the origin.
routes.partner_work: With the customer's IT or CDN team: retrieve the Edge Optimize API key; allowlist the AdobeEdgeOptimize/1.0 user agent in robots.txt and WAF or bot rules (with the fetcher key header if needed); add the routing at the outer CDN (Fastly VCL snippets, Akamai Property Manager rule, Cloudflare Worker and route, CloudFront origin and Lambda functions, Azure Front Door rule set and origin group, Apache include files); test in a lower environment with the staging key; check responses carry x-edgeoptimize-request-id; confirm routing in Brand Visibility. Guided setup (early access) can deploy the routing for Akamai, Cloudflare and CloudFront.
routes.prerequisites: Admin access to the CDN and an Edge Optimize API key from Brand Visibility. Akamai guided setup: an EdgeGrid API client with Property Manager (PAPI) read-write and rights to activate. Cloudflare: Workers enabled on the domain. CloudFront: IAM rights to create Lambda functions, IAM roles, distributions and cache policies. Apache: 2.4 or later with the modules the guide lists (proxy, proxy_http, ssl, rewrite, headers, env, setenvif).
routes.url_title: Experience League: Optimize at Edge (Adobe Brand Visibility)
