routes.mechanism: Log forwarding declared in logForwarding.yaml and deployed with an Edge Delivery config pipeline in Cloud Manager (Adobe-managed CDN).
routes.partner_work: Write the log forwarding configuration with the destination and secret pipeline variables, deploy it through an Edge Delivery pipeline (production only), and check that logs arrive.
routes.prerequisites: An Edge Delivery site in Cloud Manager on the Adobe-managed CDN; the customer's logging product or license.
routes.quote: Configure the endpoints and credentials for forwarding logs to various destinations, including Azure Blob Storage, Datadog, HTTPS, Elasticsearch, Splunk
routes.notes: The page's feature table marks log forwarding for both Publish Delivery and Edge Delivery. The detailed log forwarding page does not mention Edge Delivery, so which log types an Edge Delivery site sends is not stated.

routes.mechanism: Forms Submission Service: an Adobe-hosted service writes Edge Delivery form submissions into a spreadsheet.
routes.partner_work: Build the form, prepare the destination spreadsheet, share the project folder with forms@adobe.com as Editor, configure the submit action and test submissions.
routes.prerequisites: A Google account or a Microsoft 365 account that can create and share the spreadsheet. Experience League files these pages under AEM Forms ('Applies to AEM Forms'); whether an AEM Forms license is needed is not stated.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Forms Submission Service with Edge Delivery Services Forms
routes.quote: The Forms Submission Service is Adobe’s hosted solution that automatically stores form submission data directly in your preferred spreadsheets
routes.notes: The page points 'Enterprise integrations with databases' to other routes. aem.live's forms page also lists submit actions to email, Marketo Engage, Workfront Fusion and Salesforce; those come from AEM Forms, which is not a canvas product.

routes.category: Third-party APIs and backends (search, commerce, payments, identity)
vendors: edge workers on Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai or AWS CloudFront
routes.mechanism: Front-end API calls from blocks; edge workers on the customer's CDN as gateway or middleware; BYOM overlay for server-rendered dynamic pages.
routes.partner_work: Pick the pattern per use case (front-end call, edge worker, App Builder action for author-side jobs, BYOM overlay), build the blocks or workers, keep API secrets server side, and add identity provider flows where pages are gated.
routes.prerequisites: Developer effort; a CDN with edge compute for edge workers; the third-party API and its credentials.
routes.url_title: aem.live (Adobe Edge Delivery Services docs): Building Integrations with AEM Edge Delivery Services
routes.quote: Edge Delivery Services is designed to be a content-first platform, but many websites require data-driven functionality such as server-side-generated content, authentication, integrations with protected APIs, and Identity Provider (IDP) connections.
routes.notes: The guide says about 95% of integrations are front-end API calls and recommends edge workers on the customer's CDN for live traffic. Data stays in the source system and is fetched when pages load. Sites on the Adobe-managed CDN can use AEM Edge Functions instead (aem.live still calls them early access in a public beta; see the AEM Sites edge item).

routes.mechanism: Adobe Commerce Optimizer as the integration layer, with Adobe Commerce Storefront on Edge Delivery; or a custom integration built from the Edge Delivery boilerplate.
routes.partner_work: Choose between Commerce Optimizer and a custom integration; for custom, build the storefront on the Edge Delivery boilerplate and reuse existing commerce components for the transactional part.
routes.prerequisites: Adobe Commerce Optimizer, a separate Adobe product, for the recommended route; Adobe says integrations to commercial solutions such as Salesforce Commerce are available through the Adobe rep.
routes.quote: If you want to integrate your existing commerce solution and boost your catalog performance, Adobe’s recommendation is to use Adobe Commerce Optimizer as the modern integration layer.
routes.notes: Adobe Commerce itself is already a canvas product (commerce-eds). Commerce Optimizer is not on the canvas.

routes.mechanism: aem-embed web component: an existing app embeds Edge Delivery content (for example a shared header and footer).
routes.partner_work: Add aem-embed.js to the host app and place aem-embed tags for the shared fragments; design and content changes then flow without releases of the host app.
routes.prerequisites: Access to the host application's code.
routes.url_title: aem.live (Adobe Edge Delivery Services docs): Embedding Content in non-AEM experiences
routes.quote: In projects we often see the need to embed content in experiences that are not controlled by AEM.
routes.notes: Useful in phased migrations that run beside a legacy site.

routes.category: CDN (customer-managed, in front of Adobe's CDN)
vendors: any CDN, load balancer or WAF
routes.mechanism: Customer-managed CDN in front of the AEM-managed CDN, authenticated with the X-AEM-Edge-Key header.
routes.partner_work: Declare the edge key with a Cloud Manager config pipeline; set the customer CDN's origin, SNI, Host, X-Forwarded-Host and X-AEM-Edge-Key; add the CDN's IPs to the IP allow list; debug with the x-aem-debug header; run a load test; validate the routing with Adobe support before live traffic.
routes.prerequisites: An existing CDN that would be onerous to replace, managed by the customer with CDN engineers on call; a passed load test; publish and preview tiers only (not author); not available on sandbox programs.
routes.url_title: Experience League: CDN in AEM as a Cloud Service
routes.quote: This option is available on a case-by-case basis, particularly when customers have existing legacy integrations with a CDN provider that are hard to replace.
routes.notes: Sample configurations are given for Akamai, Amazon CloudFront and Cloudflare. With a customer CDN in front, Brand Visibility routing has to go on that outer CDN, so AXC01 (AEM managed CDN) would not apply. Geolocation headers then reflect the customer CDN.

routes.mechanism: Self-service log forwarding (logForwarding.yaml) deployed by a Cloud Manager config pipeline: AEM, Apache/Dispatcher and CDN logs.
routes.partner_work: Write logForwarding.yaml per destination with secret pipeline variables, choose which logs go where, deploy to dev, stage and production, optionally route through advanced networking, migrate any forwarding Adobe set up the legacy way, and optionally add Adobe's CDN log analysis dashboards for Splunk or ELK.
routes.prerequisites: A license with a logging vendor or a self-hosted logging product. CDN logs to Amazon S3, Dynatrace and New Relic are in beta (request access); mutual TLS is in beta.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Log Forwarding (AEM as a Cloud Service)
routes.quote: Customers with a license with a logging vendor or who host a logging product can have AEM logs (including Apache/Dispatcher) and CDN logs forwarded to the associated logging destination.
routes.notes: Configured per AEM as a Cloud Service environment, so it serves AEM Assets environments too. The CDN Log Analysis Tooling tutorial 'offers pre-built dashboards that you can integrate with the Splunk or the ELK stack'. This is the documented way AEM data lands in a customer's data lake storage (S3, Azure Blob), and it is logs, not content. SI06 reviews logs monthly but no line sets up forwarding.

routes.mechanism: OpenTelemetry (otel.yaml deployed by a config pipeline): traces, metrics and logs from the AEM application to the customer's APM endpoint over OTLP/HTTPS. Limited Availability.
routes.partner_work: Request access, pick the APM vendor and agent variant, configure otel.yaml with the endpoint and credential, deploy per environment through the config pipeline, then build dashboards and alerts.
routes.prerequisites: Limited Availability (access by email request); the customer brings its own APM endpoint; not available to HIPAA-scoped environments, Rapid Development Environments or sandboxes.
routes.quote: You can send your telemetry to any Application Performance Monitoring vendor that accepts OpenTelemetry data over OTLP/HTTPS.
routes.notes: Replaces the APM integration built into AEM as a Cloud Service. Supports dedicated egress for private endpoints. Applies to the whole AEM environment, AEM Assets included.

vendors: SaaS vendors such as a CRM that support VPN or IP allowlists
routes.mechanism: Advanced networking: VPN, dedicated egress IP address and flexible port egress, set up in Cloud Manager (UI or API).
routes.partner_work: Design the network path with the customer's network team, provision advanced networking, set up the VPN tunnels, add the dedicated IP to third-party allowlists, and point code or Dispatcher proxies at it.
routes.prerequisites: The customer's network team and VPN-capable infrastructure; access to Cloud Manager.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Configure advanced networking for AEM as a Cloud Service
routes.quote: A VPN allows connecting to an on-premise infrastructure or data center from the author, publish, or preview instances.
routes.notes: A building block, not a ready integration: it is how custom code in AEM reaches a customer database or CRM. The page adds that a VPN 'also allows connecting to SaaS vendors such as a CRM vendor that supports VPN.' Applies to AEM Assets environments too.

vendors: translation vendors with AEM connectors (Adobe Exchange partner program)
routes.mechanism: Translation Integration Framework cloud configurations; AI translation integration with an LLM provider.
routes.partner_work: Install the vendor's connector package, create cloud configurations with the vendor credentials, create framework configurations (human or machine translation, what else to translate), associate them with page roots and run translation projects; for AI translation, connect Azure OpenAI and upload style guides.
routes.prerequisites: The customer's own license with the translation vendor (Microsoft Translator needs a Microsoft license); the customer's own Azure OpenAI license and credentials for AI translation.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Configuring the Translation Integration Framework
routes.quote: The Translation Integration Framework integrates with third-party translation services to orchestrate the translation of AEM content.
routes.notes: The Microsoft Translator connector translates 'page content or assets', so it serves AEM Assets too. The AI translation page: 'Initial support connects AEM to Azure OpenAI.'

routes.mechanism: Commerce Integration Framework (CIF) add-on with an integration layer that maps the third-party APIs to Adobe Commerce GraphQL (Adobe recommends Adobe Developer Runtime for it, included in the CIF add-on for third parties).
routes.partner_work: Build or adapt the integration layer, map the catalog APIs, configure the CIF add-on so authors can pick products and build product experiences, and let performance-critical client-side components call the commerce solution directly.
routes.prerequisites: The CIF add-on for third parties; real-time catalog APIs (or an external product cache); third-party connectors are not maintained by Adobe.
routes.url_title: Experience League: AEM and third-Party Commerce Integration using Commerce Integration Framework
routes.quote: The integration of non-Adobe Commerce solution is a common scenario for CIF.
routes.notes: Adobe now says the CIF storefront is in maintenance mode and should not be used in new projects; it recommends Edge Delivery (see the Edge Delivery commerce item). A headless storefront can still use the CIF add-on to bring product data into AEM.

routes.category: Custom front ends and apps (headless delivery)
routes.mechanism: Content Fragment delivery APIs (GraphQL and OpenAPI REST), with the Universal Editor for visual editing on bring-your-own-app front ends.
routes.partner_work: Model the content fragments, enable the delivery API (OpenAPI delivery is enabled through an Adobe Support ticket), configure CORS and referrer filters, connect the front end, and instrument it for the Universal Editor.
routes.prerequisites: AEM as a Cloud Service; an Adobe Support ticket for Content Fragment Delivery with OpenAPI.
routes.url_title: Experience League: AEM APIs for Structured Content Delivery and Management
routes.quote: Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) as a Cloud Service offers multiple APIs for both structured content delivery from Content Fragments and Content Fragment management.
routes.notes: Universal Editor introduction: 'It is compatible with virtually any architecture (SSR, CSR), web framework (Next.js, React, Astro, etc.), and hosting models'. The Content Fragment Selector can also be embedded in non-Adobe applications after a provisioning ticket.

routes.mechanism: AEM MCP Server (one URL; OAuth sign-in; each tool runs with the user's own AEM permissions): create, read, update and delete pages and content fragments, plus Cloud Manager tools.
routes.partner_work: Configure the MCP client apps the customer uses, decide read-only or read-write per tool category (restrictions are requested from Adobe), and train practitioners; for changes and deletes Adobe points users to the AI Assistant, which has safeguards.
routes.prerequisites: AEM as a Cloud Service; users' existing AEM permissions apply; some tools need a minimum AEM release; the Experience Governance tools need the agents trial or a paid license.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Using MCP with AEM as a Cloud Service
routes.quote: Many Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) teams now work in Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) and chat-based applications such as Cursor, OpenAI ChatGPT, Anthropic Claude, and Microsoft Copilot Studio.
routes.notes: The supported list also has Workfront Fusion (Adobe). Step-by-step guides exist for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, JetBrains with GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Studio. The same server covers AEM Assets (see the AEM Assets item). In this product group, Snowflake's agent apps (CoCo, CoWork) and Amazon Quick are the only data-platform vendor tools Adobe names, and they call AEM tools rather than load data.

routes.category: Business systems (CRM, PIM, OMS) by events
routes.mechanism: AEM Eventing: AEM as a Cloud Service sends events (for example content fragment created, updated or deleted) to Adobe I/O Events, which pushes them to webhooks, Adobe I/O Runtime or Amazon EventBridge, or lets consumers pull them from the journal.
routes.partner_work: Enable AEM Events for the environment, set up the Adobe Developer Console project and subscriptions, build the consumer (webhook, Runtime action or EventBridge rule) that updates the outside system, and call back into AEM through its APIs where needed.
routes.prerequisites: AEM as a Cloud Service; Adobe Developer Console access; only the published event types are available.
routes.quote: AEM Eventing is a cloud-native eventing system that enables subscriptions to AEM Events for processing in external systems.
routes.notes: The page names event consumers as 'a CRM (Customer Relationship Management), PIM(Product Information Management), OMS (Order Management System), or a custom application.' Applies to AEM Assets too (see its PIM item).

routes.mechanism: SAML 2.0 authentication on AEM Publish or Preview for end users of the site.
routes.partner_work: Configure the identity provider and AEM Publish's SAML 2.0 OSGi configuration (the IDP certificate that validates assertions, user attribute sync and group membership updates), then test sign-in on the protected paths.
routes.prerequisites: The customer's SAML 2.0 identity provider; it is for site visitors, not AEM authors.
routes.url_title: Experience League: SAML 2.0 authentication (AEM as a Cloud Service tutorial)
routes.quote: SAML 2.0 integration with AEM Publish (or Preview), allows end users of an AEM-based web experience to authenticate to a non-Adobe IDP (Identity Provider), and access AEM as a named, authorized user.
routes.notes: For member or gated sites. Edge Delivery sites handle identity providers in edge workers instead (see the Edge Delivery integrations item).

vendors: Microsoft 365 Outlook (SMTP with OAuth2 or Microsoft Graph)
routes.mechanism: AEM Mail Service authenticated with OAuth2.
routes.partner_work: Register the application with the mail provider, then configure AEM's mail service with the OAuth2 settings and secrets for the chosen transport.
routes.prerequisites: The customer's email tenant and an administrator who can register the application.
routes.url_title: Experience League: OAuth2 Support for the Mail Service
routes.quote: AEM as a Cloud Service offers OAuth2 support for its integrated Mail Service to allow organizations to adhere to secure email requirements.
routes.notes: Environment-level plumbing (notifications and workflows); low priority for the canvas.

routes.mechanism: Cloud Manager external repositories linked to full-stack and front-end pipelines.
routes.partner_work: Add the repository in Cloud Manager, validate ownership (the Adobe GitHub app for github.com; an access token and webhook for the others) and link it to the pipelines.
routes.prerequisites: Cloud Manager access; an access token for non-github.com hosts.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Add external repositories in Cloud Manager
routes.quote: For AEM as a Cloud Service and Adobe Managed Services (AMS) users, the repository can be linked to both full-stack and frontend pipelines.
routes.notes: Sites Optimizer opens its code-fix pull requests on these repositories (AXC06). SI01 already sets up Git access.

routes.category: Third-party APIs and non-Adobe backends (at the CDN)
routes.mechanism: AEM Edge Functions: JavaScript on the Adobe-managed CDN that calls outside APIs; plus CDN origin selectors that route paths to non-Adobe backends.
routes.partner_work: Declare the edge function in YAML and deploy it through the configuration pipeline (calling the outside APIs with secrets kept server side), route paths to it with origin selector rules, or point origin selectors at another backend.
routes.prerequisites: A Cloud Manager program with AEM Java-stack environments or Edge Delivery sites, and a configuration pipeline (an Edge Delivery Services pipeline for Edge Delivery sites); executions are limited by the AEM as a Cloud Service product description; at most 32 backend requests per execution.
routes.quote: Reformatting or aggregating responses from third-party APIs before they reach the browser
routes.notes: 'AEM Edge Functions is compatible with both Edge Delivery Services and AEM as a Cloud Service Java-stack, for AEM Sites customers.' The config pipeline table describes origin selectors as rules 'to route traffic to different backends, including non-Adobe applications'.

routes.mechanism: Bulk Import from an external storage account (Assets view: Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, Dropbox, OneDrive; Admin view: Azure and S3), run once or on a recurring schedule.
routes.partner_work: Gather the storage credentials, create an import configuration per source folder, handle file name rules and metadata, schedule recurring runs where the source keeps changing, and monitor the executed and scheduled imports.
routes.prerequisites: Credentials for the source (Azure account and key or SAS token; AWS region, bucket and keys; GCP bucket and service account; Dropbox app key and secret; OneDrive tenant, client ID and secret); administrator rights in AEM.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Bulk import assets using Assets view
routes.quote: Scheduling imports lets you automate data ingestion so your datasets stay current without manual re-uploads.
routes.notes: The catalog's AS03 covers a one-time migration; recurring ingestion from cloud storage is not a line today. Content Hub users can also add approved assets from OneDrive or Dropbox.

vendors: any third-party system that exports CSV
routes.mechanism: Bulk metadata import and export with CSV files.
routes.partner_work: Map the outside system's fields to the AEM metadata schema, register any custom namespaces, run imports in batches outside busy hours, and export metadata to CSV when needed.
routes.prerequisites: CSV exports from the outside system; custom namespaces registered first.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Import and export asset metadata in bulk
routes.quote: You can also ingest asset metadata in bulk from third-party system in CSV format.
routes.notes: A file route, not a live connection; the event-driven PIM route is the next item.

routes.category: Product information management (PIM) and other business systems
routes.mechanism: AEM Eventing (Asset Processing Completed event) to an Adobe I/O Runtime action that calls the PIM and writes metadata back with the Assets Author API.
routes.partner_work: Enable AEM Events, subscribe to the asset event in the Developer Console, build the action that fetches SKU, supplier or product details from the PIM, and update the asset metadata in AEM.
routes.prerequisites: AEM as a Cloud Service with AEM Eventing enabled; Adobe Developer Console access; Adobe Developer CLI.
routes.url_title: Experience League: AEM Assets events for PIM integration
routes.quote: This example demonstrates how a third-party system, such as a Product Information Management (PIM) system, can be integrated with AEM as a Cloud Service Assets.
routes.notes: The page says a webhook in the third-party system or Amazon EventBridge can replace Runtime.

routes.mechanism: Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Assets Connector in Figma: place AEM assets on the Figma canvas and save designs back to AEM Assets.
routes.partner_work: Make the connector available to designers, agree the destination folders, and train designers on import, update checks and export.
routes.prerequisites: Valid AEM Assets and Figma licenses; AEM release 19149 or later.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Integrate AEM Assets with Figma
routes.quote: AEM Assets integrates natively with Figma, which allows designers to directly access the assets stored in AEM Assets from within the Figma user interface.
routes.notes: No catalog line today.

vendors: non-Adobe web applications built with React, Angular or vanilla JavaScript
routes.mechanism: Content Advisor (the asset selector micro-frontend) embedded in a non-Adobe application.
routes.partner_work: Embed Content Advisor in the host application with its IMS sign-in (the app's URL must be in the IMS client's allowed redirect URLs), have the host domains allowlisted, and set the repository, filters and Dynamic Media rendition options.
routes.prerequisites: Content Advisor access provisioned for the organization as part of the AEM Assets as a Cloud Service profile; the host domains allowlisted; a Dynamic Media license for Dynamic Media renditions.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Use Content Advisor to access AEM content in Adobe and non-Adobe applications
routes.quote: Content Advisor is also available for integration with non-Adobe (third-party) applications, extending intelligent asset discovery beyond Adobe applications.
routes.notes: Adobe's older page for the non-Adobe asset selector now redirects to a GitHub examples repository. The Dynamic Media with OpenAPI overview says: 'To integrate with a non-Adobe application, provide domain names to allow list where the application is hosted.'

routes.mechanism: AEM Content Advisor browser extension (Chrome Web Store): find approved assets and Dynamic Media renditions and drop them into any web editor.
routes.partner_work: Roll out the extension, configure its settings, and train teams; no integration code.
routes.prerequisites: An Adobe ID with access to the AEM Assets repository; a Dynamic Media license to see Dynamic Media renditions.
routes.url_title: Experience League: AEM Content Advisor browser extension
routes.quote: and third-party tools such as Google Docs/WordPress/Microsoft Powerpoint, and any other web application
routes.notes: The page sells it as 'Zero setup, zero code.'

routes.mechanism: Dynamic Media with OpenAPI: search and delivery APIs that serve approved assets by reference (delivery URLs with image modifiers, video players and manifests).
routes.partner_work: Approve assets for delivery, integrate the delivery URLs and image modifiers into the outside app, allowlist its domains, and optionally set a custom delivery domain.
routes.prerequisites: Licenses for AEM Assets as a Cloud Service and AEM Dynamic Media; Dynamic Media with OpenAPI enabled on request.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Dynamic Media with OpenAPI capabilities
routes.quote: It allows your developers to easily integrate delivery of assets with their applications. The applications include Adobe as well as third-party applications.
routes.notes: The catalog's XC13 already turns this on for Commerce; this is the same service serving a non-Adobe app.

routes.mechanism: AEM MCP Server content tools for assets: import, search, upload, download, move, copy, delete, publish and metadata edits.
routes.partner_work: Same setup as for AEM Sites: configure the MCP clients, decide read-only or read-write, train practitioners.
routes.prerequisites: AEM as a Cloud Service; users' AEM permissions apply; asset import and search need a minimum AEM release; Dynamic Media with OpenAPI for on-the-fly renditions.
routes.url_title: Experience League: Using MCP with AEM as a Cloud Service
routes.quote: There is also support for asset upload, download, move/copy/delete, and publish/unpublish for assets, along with editing metadata, inspecting references, and identifying unused assets.

not_documented: A data warehouse or lakehouse connector (Snowflake, Google BigQuery, Databricks, Amazon Redshift) for Brand Visibility, Sites Optimizer, Edge Delivery Services, AEM Sites or AEM Assets, in either direction. The nearest documented routes are AEM and Edge Delivery log forwarding to Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage (logs, not content or metrics) and Snowflake's or Amazon's agent apps calling the AEM MCP server.
An API, MCP server, scheduled export or warehouse feed for Brand Visibility or Sites Optimizer data: only CSV and PDF downloads are documented.

Brand Visibility CDN log forwarding for a site served by the AEM-managed CDN (Fastly): the Brand Visibility log guides cover customer-managed CDNs only, and AEM's log forwarding page does not name Brand Visibility as a destination.

Native Brand Visibility log forwarding guides for Azure Front Door, Apache HTTP Server, Google Cloud CDN or other CDNs: they go through Other (manual upload). Imperva has a log guide but no Optimize at Edge routing guide; Azure Front Door and Apache have routing guides but no log guide.

A Brand Visibility connector that writes fixes into a non-Adobe CMS (for example WordPress or Sitecore): Optimize at Edge applies fixes at the CDN instead and is described as working regardless of the CMS.
Connecting a customer's own Semrush, Ahrefs or Bing Webmaster Tools account to Brand Visibility or Sites Optimizer: Semrush and Ahrefs data come built in, and Bing is not mentioned.
Google Analytics or any web analytics tool in Sites Optimizer: its settings page has only Google Search Console and Connect to AEM Sites.
How Sites Optimizer connects to Jira (setup steps, permissions): only release notes mention it, as Early Access.
Sites Optimizer for an Edge Delivery site whose code is not on GitHub: the Connect to AEM Sites guide asks only for a GitHub URL.
Ready-made Edge Delivery content-source connectors for other CMSs (for example WordPress, Sitecore, Contentful or Drupal): only the generic Bring Your Own Markup API is documented.

Exporting Edge Delivery or AEM Operational Telemetry to an outside analytics tool or warehouse: Adobe's knowledge base article on the RUM script points customers to the Operational Telemetry Explorer and says a unique list of referrer URLs cannot be exported directly.
Which log types an Edge Delivery site forwards: the config pipeline table allows log forwarding for Edge Delivery, but the log forwarding page itself does not mention Edge Delivery.
Whether Edge Delivery forms (Forms Submission Service) need an AEM Forms license: the pages are filed under AEM Forms but do not say.
Connecting AEM Assets to a third-party DAM (for example Bynder or Aprimo): Connected Assets is documented only between Experience Manager deployments.

Adobe-documented AEM Assets connectors for Microsoft 365, Microsoft Teams, Salesforce or Canva: none found on Experience League (the Content Advisor browser extension covers Google Docs, WordPress and PowerPoint in the browser).
A CRM connector for AEM Sites, AEM Assets or Edge Delivery outside AEM Forms: CRM is reached only through generic routes (AEM Eventing, VPN or dedicated egress, edge functions, front-end API calls).

Outside integrations listed only on business.adobe.com (the AEM Assets and AEM Sites integrations pages): the site refused automated reads (HTTP 503 and empty replies on Nov 2, as on Oct 31), so anything listed only there is not covered here.
sites.summary:
I found 45 documented routes from Brand Visibility (7), Sites Optimizer (8), Edge Delivery Services (9), AEM Sites (13) and AEM Assets (8) to systems that are not Adobe products. A script checked every quote word for word against a downloaded copy of its Adobe page, plus every quoted phrase in the notes, and found no em or en dashes (ALL ITEM CHECKS PASSED). Files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-warroom/432cd4fe-7682-5283-bb86-965652091bf2/scratchpad/outside/content_group/ (items.json, scripts/items.py, scripts/verify.py, pages/).

Outside pieces that come up again and again, and would suit optional boxes that are off by default:
1. Customer CDN (Akamai, Cloudflare, Fastly, CloudFront; Brand Visibility also covers Imperva, Azure Front Door and Apache). One box touches three products, with different work for each:
   - Brand Visibility: logs flow into Adobe's S3 bucket, which unlocks Agentic and Referral Traffic. Optimize at Edge routing goes on the outer CDN.
   - Edge Delivery: a BYO production CDN with push invalidation.
   - AEM Sites: a customer CDN placed in front of Adobe's CDN, allowed case by case.
   The catalog already covers parts of this (L02, C07, AXC01). A CDN box could take over C07, which today sits only on bv-commerce, so no hours are added.
2. Content source and Git.
   - SharePoint or Google Drive: Edge Delivery content, Sites Optimizer fixes written back into the documents, and form submissions. A customer SharePoint needs an Azure app registration and tenant admin consent, which is customer IT work just like CDN logs.
   - GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps: Edge Delivery code, AEM pipelines and Sites Optimizer pull requests.
3. Google Search Console and Google Analytics 4.
   - Search Console: Brand Visibility prompt suggestions and Sites Optimizer SEO data. These are two separate connections.
   - Google Analytics 4: Brand Visibility's Business Impact tab, on the paid offer only.
4. Cloud storage into AEM Assets: Azure Blob, S3, Google Cloud, Dropbox and OneDrive bulk import. It can now run on a recurring schedule, which makes it the nearest thing in this group to outside data being ingested. AS03 covers only a one-time migration.
5. Logs and monitoring.
   - Out of Adobe: AEM, and Edge Delivery through its config pipeline, forward logs to Splunk, Datadog, Dynatrace, New Relic, Sumo Logic, Elasticsearch, HTTPS, S3 or Azure Blob. OpenTelemetry can send to any OTLP monitoring tool (limited availability).
   - Into Brand Visibility: logs held in Splunk or Elasticsearch get there only through the manual Other upload.
6. Business systems:
   - AEM Eventing sends AEM Sites and Assets events to webhooks or Amazon EventBridge for a CRM, PIM or OMS. Adobe's PIM example writes SKU data back into asset metadata.
   - A VPN or dedicated egress IP reaches on-premise databases.
   - Third-party commerce goes through a CIF integration layer, or Commerce Optimizer on Edge Delivery.
   - Also documented: translation vendors (Microsoft Translator, Adobe Exchange connectors, Azure OpenAI), SAML identity providers and Figma.
   - Content Advisor can be embedded in third-party apps, and a browser extension works in Google Docs, WordPress and PowerPoint.
   - Dynamic Media with OpenAPI delivers assets to non-Adobe apps.
   - aem-embed puts Edge Delivery content into non-AEM sites.
7. AI assistants: the AEM MCP server works with Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Amazon Quick, Snowflake CoWork and coding tools, for AEM Sites and Assets content.

Built in, so not boxes: Semrush inside Brand Visibility and Ahrefs inside Sites Optimizer.

Data warehouses: none of these five products documents a Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks or Redshift connector in either direction. Brand Visibility and Sites Optimizer have no data API, only CSV and PDF downloads. For this group, the warehouse and data lake question belongs to the Experience Platform products on the canvas, not to these.

Optional: campaign sync and custom object sync.

routes.quote: Use LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms to run ad campaigns in LinkedIn and generate leads for Marketo.

Facebook Lead Ads page (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/marketo/using/product-docs/demand-generation/facebook/set-up-facebook-lead-ads): 'To get Facebook Lead Ads added to your instance, contact the Adobe Account Team (your Account Manager).'

routes.mechanism: Customer Attributes (Experience Cloud People service): a CSV keyed on the customer ID, uploaded in the browser (up to 100 MB) or by FTP or SFTP (up to 4 GB, with a .fin file), schema validation, then a subscription for Target.
routes.partner_work: Export CRM data to CSV, create the attribute source and alias, upload by HTTPS or FTP/SFTP, validate the schema, subscribe Target and activate the source, and pass the same customer ID on the site (mbox3rdPartyId) so profiles match; then build audiences and profile scripts on the attributes.
routes.prerequisites: Users in the Customer Attributes group plus an Analytics or Target group; Customer Attributes listed as a product profile in the Admin Console; Experience Cloud ID; at.js (any version). Up to 5 attributes for Target Standard and 200 for Target Premium.
routes.quote: Enterprise customer data collected through multiple sources and stored inside CRM databases can be used in Target to strategically deliver the most relevant content to customers, specifically focusing on returning customers.
routes.notes: Adobe 'does not guarantee that 100% of customer attribute (visitor profile) data from CRM databases will be onboarded'. The data lives as long as the Target visitor profile, 14 days by default. The at.js to Web SDK comparison lists Customer attributes as supported on both. Upload steps: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/core-services/interface/services/customer-attributes/t-crs-usecase.

routes.mechanism: Bulk Profile Update API (v2): HTTP POST of a batch file of profile attributes keyed on the Target ID or mbox3rdPartyId.
routes.partner_work: Export attributes from the CRM or POS, build the batch file (batch= header, URL-encoded values), post it, check batch status, and optionally require a profile authentication token.
routes.prerequisites: Batch file under 50 MB and at most 500,000 rows; the TNT ID or mbox3rdPartyId. All external profile data for a visitor must not exceed 64 KB.
routes.url_title: Bulk Profile Update API (Adobe Target developer guide)
routes.quote: External sources can include Customer Relationship Management (CRM) or Point of Sale (POS) systems, which are not usually available on a web page.
routes.notes: Usable only in Target, unlike Customer Attributes, which Analytics can also use. v2 creates profiles Target has not seen; v1 updates existing profiles only. The Profile API settings page lets admins require an access token for batch updates. API reference: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/target-dev/developer/api/profile-apis/profile-bulk-api.

routes.mechanism: Single Profile Update API: one profile update per call, sent when an offline event happens.
routes.partner_work: Call the API from the system where the event happens (call center, lending, loyalty, kiosk), keyed on the visitor's third-party ID.
routes.prerequisites: A visitor ID (mbox3rdPartyId) shared between the outside system and the site.
routes.url_title: Single Profile Update API (Adobe Target developer guide)
routes.quote: Actions can include reaching a call center, a loan is funded, using a loyalty card in store, accessing a kiosk, and so forth.
routes.notes: Same page: 'generally used when an update must occur in relation to a transaction occurring in a channel that has not implemented Target'.

routes.mechanism: at.js Data Providers (targetGlobalSettings): browser code fetches outside data and passes it to Target as mbox parameters.
routes.partner_work: Write each provider function (sync or async, with timeout and caching), define it before at.js loads, and build audiences on the new parameters.
routes.prerequisites: at.js 1.3 or later; an account with the data provider.
routes.quote: This setting lets customers gather data from third-party data providers, such as Demandbase, BlueKai, and custom services, and pass the data to Target as mbox parameters in the global mbox request.
routes.notes: With Platform Web SDK, which TG01 on the canvas assumes, the migration comparison says Data Providers are 'Not supported. Custom code can be used to trigger a Platform Web SDK sendEvent command after data is retrieved from another provider.' (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/platform-learn/migrate-target-to-websdk/detailed-comparison). The at.js integrations page names 'Third-party data providers (e.g. Demandbase, Bluekai, weather APIs)'.

routes.mechanism: Recommendations feeds: CSV or Google Product Feed files pulled from a customer-hosted FTP or FTPS, SFTP or URL location on a daily, weekly or every-two-weeks schedule.

routes.prerequisites: Target Premium (Recommendations). A customer-hosted server: 'Adobe does not host an SFTP endpoint, use a customer-hosted server.'
routes.quote: Use feeds to get entities imported into Adobe Target Recommendations.
routes.notes: Already on the canvas as optional TG04. Entities expire after 61 days. The SFTP section still says 'The production IP list must be confirmed by engineering before publication of this update', so Adobe's download addresses are not yet published there.

routes.mechanism: Recommendations Save Entities API (a Target Admin API) to add or update items, for example when inventory or price crosses a threshold.
routes.partner_work: Set up Adobe Developer Console authentication for the Target Admin APIs and call Save Entities from the source system alongside the feed.
routes.prerequisites: Target Premium; Target Admin API authentication through Adobe Developer Console; the Target environment ID.
routes.url_title: Manage your Recommendations catalog using APIs (Adobe Target)
routes.quote: To populate your Recommendations product database using the API rather than a CSV product feed or Target requests firing on product pages, use the Save Entities API
routes.notes: The page describes a JWT token flow; check the current Adobe Developer Console credential type before building. Target API overview: 'all Admin APIs require authentication.'

routes.mechanism: Recommendations custom criteria: a CSV of keys and recommended items pulled from FTP or FTPS, SFTP or a URL.
routes.partner_work: Export the outside model's results in Adobe's CSV template, host the file, create the custom criteria, and monitor the sync status.

routes.notes: Up to 1,000 recommended items per key. 'Custom criteria feeds update once every 24 hours.' Keys missing from a new upload expire 31 days after their last upload.

marketo-workfront-target.summary: 47 documented routes for this group: Marketo Engage 17, Workfront 18, Target 12. Outside systems are normal for all three products and Adobe documents them well, so an outside-system piece on the canvas (off by default in the plays, available to add) is well supported here. Picking by category (CRM, data warehouse, cloud storage, ad platform, webinar, BI, chat, any API) with the vendors listed inside fits the docs better than one box per vendor. Strongest candidates: Marketo with CRM (already MK02), ad platforms (audiences out, leads in, offline conversions), webinar platforms, warehouse via the bulk APIs, and webhooks; Workfront with Fusion apps (one license gate) and Data Connect to Snowflake and BI; Target with CRM and POS data (Customer Attributes, profile APIs) and catalog feeds (already TG04). Low priority: Sales Insight Actions mailboxes, Box picks in Design Studio, non-Adobe tag managers. Data warehouses: Marketo sends data out through the Bulk Extract API ("ETL, data warehousing, and archival workflows") or the Lead Activity Data Stream and takes data in through Bulk Import or the Data Ingestion API, with no native Snowflake or BigQuery share. Workfront sends data out through Data Connect (Snowflake reader account, BI tools, and now a Snowflake private listing) and has no inbound warehouse connector. Target has no warehouse route of its own; the only documented one is Experience Platform Federated Audience Composition audiences activated to the Adobe Target destination, which belongs with Real-Time CDP. License and access gates (no prices): Workfront Fusion is included with Workfront Ultimate and an extra purchase for Select or Prime (legacy license: Workfront Fusion for Work Automation and Integration), and it opens 53 third-party apps plus HTTP, SOAP, FTP and SFTP; the Data Connect pages list the Ultimate package; Marketo's Data Ingestion API needs the Performance Tier package and its data streams a Performance or Ultimate tier; Marketo custom objects and the Google AdWords offline-conversion sync are sold separately; Vibes SMS needs an Adobe license; Facebook Lead Ads is added by the Adobe Account Team; Target Premium is needed for the Recommendations routes and for 200 customer attributes (Standard gets 5); the warehouse route to Target needs the Federated Audience Composition add-on. Watch-outs: at.js Data Providers do not work on Platform Web SDK, which TG01 assumes; Workfront for Jira and Workfront for Outlook are retired; Workfront custom OAuth2 apps could not be created after November 1, 2026 and stop working February 1, 2027. Flag, not fixed: Workfront Fusion has Adobe Target modules ("Adobe Target modules allow you to create, read, update, or delete records", https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/workfront-fusion/using/references/apps-and-their-modules/adobe-connectors/adobe-target-modules), an Adobe-to-Adobe link that is not among the catalog's 59 connections (there is no workfront-target). Doc oddities: the Target feeds page says Adobe's SFTP IP list "must be confirmed by engineering", and the Target catalog API page still describes a JWT token flow. Adobe publishes no hours for any of this, so any service lines would be our estimates.
